blocks.content: The equilibrium line marks the crucial structural boundary on a glacier where annual snow accumulation precisely balances annual ice loss.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A glacier is structurally divided into the Zone of Accumulation (upper region with net ice gain) and the Zone of Ablation (lower region with net ice loss).
The Equilibrium Line Altitude (ELA) represents the exact boundary where annual snow accumulation equals annual ablation.
The upper 50 meters of a glacier undergoes brittle deformation, creating deep fractures known as crevasses, while deeper ice flows via plastic deformation.
Glacial till and debris are organized into moraines: lateral moraines along the sides, medial moraines where glaciers merge, and terminal moraines at the snout.

rows: Covered by perennial firn and snow

items: UPSC/State PSC Question: Medial moraines are formed when two lateral moraines unite at the confluence of two joining valley glaciers.
Plastic vs Brittle Flow: Remember that crevasses only extend to about 50 meters depth because hydrostatic pressure causes ice below this point to deform plastically.
Glacial Terminus: The snout of a glacier frequently feeds proglacial lakes or meltwater river origins (e.g., Gaumukh at the Gangotri Glacier).
